newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOOSNAM TAKES EARLY LEAD AFTER FIRING A 68.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOOSNAM TAKES EARLY LEAD AFTER FIRING A 68.

text.p: Ian Woosnam charged to the head of the field early in the second round of the British PGA Championship on Saturday by defying a swirling wind to shoot a four-under-par 68.
Woosnam's round took him to 135, nine under par on the 6,957-yard Wentworth course and three strokes better than his playing partner, reigning European number one Colin Montgomerie.
Montgomerie recorded his second successive three-under-par 69, helped by chip-ins for birdies at the 13th and 14th, but was disappointed not to birdie either of the last two par-fives.
Trinidad's Stephen Ames and Frank Nobilo of New Zealand shared third place among the early finishers on five under par after rounds of 69 and 71 respectively.
Meanwhile, Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros withdrew from the tournament with a bad back before even beginning his second round.
Ballesteros, who shot 76 in Friday's opening round, struck a few practice shots on the driving range but then said his back was too sore to continue and withdrew.

The first round leaders at six under, Irishmen Eamonn Darcy and Darren Clarke, had not begun their rounds when Woosnam and Montgomerie finished. Nor had Bernhard Langer, Ernie Els or Nick Faldo, all contenders after the opening day.
Woosnam dropped shots at the second hole after three-putting from the fringe, and at the third where he three-putted from 90 feet.
But he birdied the fourth and ninth holes on putts of 15 and 20 feet and then collected further birdies at the 12th, 13th, 16th and 18th.
He holed from 15 feet at the last and has only two putts on that green in two days. He sank a 55-footer for eagle in his opening 67.
Woosnam continued to be happy with his shorter, 32-inch putter. "I moved my hands a bit higher and I seemed to have a little more control," he said.
"Today was tricky in the wind. You had to keep the ball low because if you got up over the trees, it could go anywhere."
Montgomerie said his two chip-ins made his round.
The first was routine but the second, from the slope behind the 14th just 15 feet away, was fortunate.
"It bounced in the fringe and would have rolled off the front of the green but it hit the pin and dropped in," he said.
Montgomerie said he should have had at least one birdie at the last two dog-leg par-fives. At 17 he drove perfectly and was 50 yards short of the green in two.
His chip covered 40 yards, leaving him another chip which he hit six feet past and he had to hole that for par.
He drove into the rough at 18 and needed a four-footer to salvage par.
"Two 69s round here is not bad," said Montgomerie, the biggest name in the field not to have won at Wentworth, either in this event or the World Matchplay.
